core_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year. It's been an eye-opening experience that has given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I was initially hesitant, but it turned out to be a great decision.

archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year. It's been an eye-opening experience that has given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I was initially hesitant, but it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.research_lab: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. My main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.first_research_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to explore specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored a paper on this system, which was a surreal and proud moment for me.
archival_memory.current_research: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can enhance scientists' understanding of complex data. It's a leap from traditional coding and data visualization. I'm experimenting with integrating VR headsets, using engines like Unity or Unreal, and finding efficient ways to stream data into 3D environments. It's cutting-edge work, and I'm forging my own path as there isn't a well-established library for VR data visualization yet.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding; it's also about reading and staying up-to-date with the latest developments in your field. I spend a significant amount of time reading academic papers, conference proceedings, and workshops to find solutions to specific problems. It can be overwhelming, but I've learned to skim through papers effectively by focusing on the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Sharing interesting findings with the lab and discussing how to incorporate them into our workflow is a great way to collaborate and improve our own processes.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep knowledge in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their passion and dedication. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets, which can be integrated with our VR platform. This would allow us to display a compressed representation of datasets like climate data, improving real-time performance. Working alongside him and other students provides valuable insights into how theoretical concepts are applied in real-world scenarios. Spontaneous brainstorming sessions, like those over coffee in the lab break room, often lead to innovative ideas and solutions.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research through poster presentations at smaller symposiums around campus. It's a great experience that requires distilling complex research into visually engaging and easy-to-understand materials. Initially, I was nervous about facing tough questions from professors or industry professionals. However, the reality was quite different. People were genuinely interested in our work and engaged in friendly dialogues. I even met a few individuals from local startups who shared valuable insights on how VR for data visualization could be applied in commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. These interactions opened my eyes to the potential real-world applications of our research.
archival_memory.publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission. The conference we're targeting is the IEEE Visualization Conference(IEEE VIS), which is a significant event in our field. Our research focuses on comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment through a user study. We believe that VR immersion enables researchers to identify anomalies or trends more quickly than with a plain 2D chart. To support this hypothesis, we conducted a small user trial with 15 participants, recording their times and gathering UX feedback. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with different team members handling specific sections. I'm responsible for the system architecture and prototype design, while others are working on the user study methodology and our PI is integrating everything into a cohesive narrative. Balancing this with my senior coursework and capstone project is a challenge, but it's a valuable learning experience.
archival_memory.grad_school_plans: I'm currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. I believe that gaining practical experience in product development will help me better understand the relevance of cutting-edge concepts like data visualization and machine learning. My mentor suggested that industry experience can provide a valuable perspective on real-world problems, making me a more practical researcher if I decide to return for a PhD. It's a great way to balance theory and application.
archival_memory.challenges_in_research: Research can be frustrating at times, with weeks spent on approaches that don't pan out or discovering that your idea has already been done and improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate existing findings into your work. By reading existing papers, thinking of new angles or applications, and pushing boundaries, you can contribute to the ever-growing foundation of knowledge. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special, as it allows us to build upon each other's work and create something innovative.
archival_memory.lab_crisis: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost vital data that wasn't fully backed up. It was a frantic night of email chains and Zoom calls with the lab manager as everyone scrambled to see if we could recover the data. Fortunately, we managed to restore most of it. However, that crisis taught us the importance of data backups and led us to set up a better backup system with checks to prevent relying on a single point of failure. It was a stressful experience, but it also brought the lab together and made us more resilient.
archival_memory.research_connections: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student in their classes. My PI is very approachable and supportive, and I can easily reach out to her for guidance on career direction or help with academic struggles. She has also been instrumental in recommending me for various scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. One such opportunity was a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I had the chance to engage with academic experts from around the world. Witnessing their debates on technical details, proposing new frameworks, and seeing them exchange ideas was truly fascinating. It felt like I was at the forefront of CS knowledge, observing the latest advancements in real time.
archival_memory.research_journey: My research journey has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that my work in the lab could shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're exploring have the potential to become standard tools, and I'm excited to be part of this pioneering effort. The sense of contributing to something bigger is what motivates me. Whether or not I pursue a graduate degree soon, this experience has changed my perspective on computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the people I've met along the way.
